mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower financing costs for corporate investments.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months with declining FEDFUNDS values.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate revenue growth concerns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate broad-based consumer demand weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations deteriorate across multiple sectors.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 250), a monthly increase in the consumer price index signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive monetary policy and depress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 250.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly payroll employment signals a robust labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as market participants price in stronger economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months with rising PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production below 105.0 (index 2017=100) indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output and profit margins, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of weak quarterly GDP growth (below 1.5% annualized) and declining housing starts signals a broad economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate investment and consumer confidence across multiple demand channels.
failure_condition: The joint condition of GDPC1 < 1.5% and HOUST decline produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses short-term discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants rapidly adjust to lower financing costs for equity valuation.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances with declining FEDFUNDS values.
